neighbours.label: an emotion or attitude adjective placed before the people it describes ('an appreciative audience', 'anxious parents', 'an angry crowd'), as against physical or neutral adjectives in the same slot
fire: After the final aria, the appreciative crowd rose to its feet.
Outside the courthouse, a resentful group of farmers waited for the verdict.
The doctor spoke softly to the fearful children before the injection.
A distrustful public ignored the minister's promises about prices.
The adoring fans screamed as the band stepped off the bus.
Reporters faced a skeptical audience at the morning briefing.
Hundreds of anxious relatives gathered at the airport for news of the flight.
The coach calmed his frightened players at halftime.
quiet: After the final aria, the large crowd rose to its feet.
Outside the courthouse, a small group of farmers waited for the verdict.
The doctor spoke softly to the young children before the injection.
A rural public ignored the minister's promises about prices.
The local fans screamed as the band stepped off the bus.
Reporters faced a crowded room at the morning briefing.
Hundreds of distant relatives gathered at the airport for the reunion.
The coach gathered his taller players at halftime.

predictions: fire 0.3-0.85 on prenominal attitude adjectives (strongest on suffix pieces like 'iative', 'ful'); size/age/location adjectives below 0.15, predicative emotion words weaker
notes: Card: 'apprec|iative' audience, 'distrust|ful', 'af|raid', ' anxious', 'disbelie|ving' public, ' frightened', 'ad|oring' parents.
